title: Robot drops or lags during a match
summary: Robot stays on the schedule but cuts out, drops, or gets laggy during matches.

options.label: Robot loses connection or cuts out
Robot stays connected but is laggy or slow to respond

drops.title: Robot loses connection during matches
steps: Check for loose power or Ethernet wires at the radio. Reseat them. A loose connection drops the link under vibration.

Check the DS log battery voltage. The radio runs down to about 4.5 V, so a brownout rarely resets it. The roboRIO browns out and disables outputs first: 6.3 V on the roboRIO 1, 6.75 V by default on the roboRIO 2 (roboRIO 2 is configurable).
Dual power is usually fine and redundant. If the radio reboots, try removing one of PoE or the DC input, since dual power can occasionally cause odd issues.

steps.text: Does the robot still drop in matches?

steps: Check the radio signal strength during the match: bars on the field monitor (FMS or FTA Buddy), or dB in the FMS station log.

steps.no: Keep working this robot's power and wiring.

steps: Low signal is the radio or the RF path. Use the lag branch of this guide for signal and the RF environment.

lag-check.question: Check the radio signal strength and trip time during the match (bars on the field monitor or FTA Buddy, dB in the FMS station log). What do you see?

options.label: Low signal or high trip time
Signal and trip time look normal

rf-environment.title: Low signal or high trip time: the RF path
steps: The link, not the robot, is the problem. Check the radio is at the top of the robot, in the open, away from motors and metal.
View the match logs in the FTA Buddy app if the extension is set up on the field. Check whether other robots in the match also had low signal or dropped packets.

steps.text: Did the whole field see it?
steps.yes: It is the field or RF environment, not this robot.

steps: Scan the 6 GHz spectrum near the field for rogue access points crowding the channel.
Rule out outside interference. A nearby airport's radar or an aircraft on approach has disrupted a field before. Watch whether the drops repeat with an outside event.

code-lag.title: Link is fine but the robot lags
steps: The radio link is fine, so the lag is in the robot or its code.
View the Driver Station log for roboRIO CPU usage and console messages about loop overruns.

steps.text: Is CPU high or are there loop overrun messages?
steps.yes: Fix the robot code. Use the Code and deploy guide, CPU branch.

steps: Look at the specific mechanism that lags: its sensors, its command, and any blocking calls in the code.
